# Adjudication Task — Chapter 278

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃278화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|아름답던 2층 주택은 흉가(凶家)로 변해 있었다.
  6|
  7|수십 겹의 방어막이 멸염신권의 충격을 일부 흡수하지 않았다면 모두 잿더미가 되어 버렸을 것이다.
  8|
  9|그때, 등 뒤로 인기척이 가까워지더니 나직한 목소리가 귓가를 울렸다.
 10|
 11|“진태경 씨.”
 12|
 13|반쯤 그을린 소파에 앉아 있던 나는 고개를 돌리며 대답했다.
 14|
 15|“네.”
 16|
 17|최 팀장과 김 집사. 그리고 송송이다.
 18|
 19|나를 바라보는 그들의 눈빛은 복잡해 보였다. 정원에서부터 처참하게 널브러진 시신들을 봤으니 당연한 반응일지도 모른다.
 20|
 21|온통 피를 뒤집어쓴 내 몰골도 썩 좋아 보이진 않을 거고.
 22|
 23|송송이가 조심스럽게 물었다.
 24|
 25|“혹시, 전부 죽인 거야?”
 26|
 27|“응.”
 28|
 29|“……!”
 30|
 31|“농담이야. 항복한 놈들은 살려 뒀어.”
 32|
 33|부드럽게 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 34|
 35|“일단은.”
 36|
 37|송송이에게 한 대답이지만 최 팀장과 김 집사를 향한 말이기도 하다.
 38|
 39|최 팀장이 우려 섞인 표정으로 물었다.
 40|
 41|“다친 곳은 없습니까?”
 42|
 43|“보시다시피 멀쩡해요.”
 44|
 45|“생존자들은?”
 46|
 47|“한곳에 모아 놨습니다.”
 48|
 49|“아무런 조치도 없이 말입니까?”
 50|
 51|“물론 했죠. 앞으로 몇 시간 동안은 숨 쉬는 시체나 다름없으니까 안심하세요.”
 52|
 53|개인적인 조치라는 건 점혈이었다.
 54|
 55|아혈과 마혈, 수혈을 짚은 뒤 블랙 헌터들을 딱 하나 남은 방에 차곡차곡 처박아 뒀다.
 56|
 57|무력 진압을 하긴 했지만, 내가 무슨 피에 미친 살인귀도 아니고 항복하는 놈들까지 죽일 생각은 없었다.
 58|
 59|무엇보다 나중에 쓰임새가 있을 수도 있고.
 60|
 61|“잘하셨습니다. 그런데…….”
 62|
 63|최 팀장의 시선이 내 발밑에 쓰러져 있는 누군가를 향했다.
 64|
 65|“그건 누굽니까?”
 66|
 67|“이 집 주인이요.”
 68|
 69|발로 놈의 몸을 뒤집자 40대 남성의 모습이 드러났다.
 70|
 71|집주인이자 블랙 헌터들의 우두머리인 임영준이다.
 72|
 73|시체로 착각할 만큼 전신이 피범벅이었지만, 분명히 살아 있다. 그것도 상처 하나 없는 모습으로.
 74|
 75|놈을 살핀 김 집사가 알 만하다는 듯이 중얼거렸다.
 76|
 77|“포션을 썼군요. 그것도 여러 번 반복해서.”
 78|
 79|“네.”
 80|
 81|“고문을 하신 겁니까?”
 82|
 83|“눈썰미가 좋으시네요.”
 84|
 85|“대격변 당시에는 흔한 일이었습니다. 블랙 헌터보다 더한 놈들도 많았고요.”
 86|
 87|고문이라는 말에 송송이의 안색이 흐려진다. 하지만 이내 옅은 한숨을 내쉬며 내 어깨에 손을 올렸다.
 88|
 89|“고생했어.”
 90|
 91|거부감이 드는 건 당연하다. 마음이 편치 않은 건 무림에 익숙한 나도 마찬가지니까.
 92|
 93|하지만 임영준은 생각했던 것 이상으로 입이 무거운 놈이었고, 어지간한 협박으로는 놈의 입을 열지 못했을 것이다.
 94|
 95|“보통 놈들이 아닙니다. 누군가는 반드시 해야 할 일이었어요.”
 96|
 97|“진태경 헌터님이 하지 않았다면 제가 했을 겁니다. 너무 괘념치 마십시오.”
 98|
 99|최 팀장과 김 집사가 각자 한마디씩을 보탰다.
100|
101|맞다. 그들의 말처럼 누군가는 해야 하는 일이었다. 이미 내 손에 피를 묻힌 마당에 고문을 망설일 이유는 없다.
102|
103|고개를 흔들어 심란한 마음을 털어 낸 내가 입을 열었다.
104|
105|“물증은 없어요. 제가 침입하고 경보 마법이 울리자마자 관련된 정보를 모두 삭제했다더군요.”
106|
107|“전부 말입니까?”
108|
109|“네. 집에는 컴퓨터도 없고, 휴대폰은 임영준을 포함해서 단 두 사람만 가지고 있었어요. 그마저도 출처를 알 수 없는 대포폰이고.”
110|
111|나는 미리 챙겨 둔 휴대폰의 잔해를 보여 주었다.
112|
113|이쪽으로는 장님이나 다름없는 내가 봐도 복구가 불가능해 보인다. 부품은 죄다 으스러졌고 SD카드는 불에 태웠다고 했으니까.
114|
115|잔해를 본 최 팀장이 작게 혀를 찼다.
116|
117|“철두철미하군요. 이 정도면 서류 같은 게 남아 있을 리 없을 테고.”
118|
119|“네.”
120|
121|“다른 블랙 헌터들은요?”
122|
123|“열 명이 살아남았는데, 하나같이 아는 사실이 없어요. 부팀장 격인 놈은 저한테 죽었고. 여기 있었던 놈들 전부 임영준이 포섭하고 훈련시켰답니다.”
124|
125|파악한 바에 의하면 놈들은 철저한 점조직 형태로 움직였다.
126|
127|신분 세탁부터 보수 지급까지. 블랙 헌터의 모든 것들은 임영준을 통해 이루어지고 있었다.
128|
129|“그나마 임영준이 살아 있었으니 다행입니다. 그가 무슨 말을 했습니까?”
130|
131|“그건…….”
132|
133|나는 문득 말을 멈췄다.
134|
135|세 번의 분근착골(分筋錯骨)을 겪은 그가 비명처럼 외친 한 마디가 아직도 귓가를 맴돌고 있었다.
136|
137|
138|
139|‘며, 명동 길드! 명동 길드라고!’
140|
141|
142|
143|국내에서 열 손가락은 자신할 수 없어도 20위 안에는 충분히 꼽히는 대형 길드. 그리고…….
144|
145|‘지훈이.’
146|
147|얼마 전 다시 만난 오랜 친구가 소속된 길드이기도 하다.
148|
149|나는 고민 끝에 다시 입을 열었다.
150|
151|“잠깐만 시간을 줄 수 있을까요?”
152|
153|“……?”
154|
155|“개인적으로 확인해 볼 문제가 있어서요.”
156|
157|물끄러미 나를 바라보던 최 팀장이 고개를 끄덕였다.
158|
159|“우선 현장을 정리하겠습니다. 확인해 보시고 알려 주세요.”
160|
161|“네.”
162|
163|“바로 시작하시죠.”
164|
165|최 팀장의 말에 김 집사가 지팡이처럼 짚고 있던 스태프를 휘둘렀다.
166|
167|굳게 닫혀 있던 방문이 열리며 혈도가 짚인 열 명의 블랙 헌터들이 공중으로 붕 떠서 차례차례 집 밖을 빠져나갔다.
168|
169|그들 사이에 임영준이 포함되어 있음은 물론이다.
170|
171|“모두 물러서십시오.”
172|
173|낮은 목소리로 경고한 김 집사가 주문을 읊었다.
174|
175|마나가 출렁임과 동시에 거대한 화염이 간신히 형태를 유지하고 있던 2층 주택을 집어삼켰다.
176|
177|불길은 정원까지 휩쓸었고 모든 것을 말소하기 전까지는 멈추지 않을 것이다.
178|
179|화르르륵!
180|
181|불과 함께 매캐한 연기구름이 솟구친다.
182|
183|그러나 저택이 위치한 한적한 시골 마을의 평화는 깨지지 않았다.
184|
185|마법으로 모든 시야와 소리가 차단된 저택은 한참 후에야 발견되겠지.
186|
187|“이걸로 될까요?”
188|
189|“이 정도면 충분합니다. 우리가 아니어도 놈들이 나서서 이곳의 존재를 지울 테니까요.”
190|
191|하루아침에 사람이 사라지고 집이 불탔지만, 그뿐이다.
192|
193|한동안 마을 사람들의 입에 오르내릴 뿐 아무 문제도 일어나지 않을 것이다.
194|
195|그것이 힘과 권력을 가진 괴물들의 방식이니까.
196|
197|다만 내가 궁금한 것은 하나였다.
198|
199|
200|
201|[가람중 동창 박지훈]
202|
203|
204|
205|지금 내 휴대폰에 저장된 이 번호의 주인은 도대체 어느 쪽일까.
206|
207|
208|
209|* * *
210|
211|
212|
213|채 어둠이 가시지 않은 새벽. 박지훈은 옷을 차려입고 집을 나섰다.
214|
215|입구에는 정복 차림의 리무진 기사가 그를 기다리고 있었다.
216|
217|“오셨습니까.”
218|
219|“무슨 일이에요? 이런 시간에 갑자기.”
220|
221|“저는 잘 모르겠습니다. 그저 댁에 가서 모셔오라는 길드장님의 지시를 받았습니다.”
222|
223|하긴. 일개 운전기사가 뭘 알겠나.
224|
225|작게 혀를 찬 박지훈은 차에 몸을 실었다. 아직 이른 새벽이라 그런지 도로는 한산했다.
226|
227|얼마나 흘렀을까. 부드럽게 내달리던 리무진은 고급 아파트와 빌라가 즐비한 한남동 모처에 정지했다.
228|
229|거대한 저택. 돌담을 따라 경비를 서고 있던 경호원 중 하나가 달려와 박지훈에게 고개를 숙인다.
230|
231|“안에서 기다리고 계십니다.”
232|
233|박지훈은 유럽 귀족 저택을 연상케 하는 철제 대문을 지나고, 운동장보다 넓은 정원을 가로지르고 난 후에야 자신을 호출한 사람을 만날 수 있었다.
234|
235|“아침 먹었나?”
236|
237|그는 반백의 50대 장년인이었다. 나이가 무색하게 체구는 당당했고, 흰색 가운 너머로 잘 발달된 가슴 근육이 보였다.
238|
239|박지훈은 고개를 숙이며 대답했다.
240|
241|“아직 식전입니다.”
242|
243|“그럼 와서 들게. 오늘 소고기 뭇국이 아주 잘 됐어.”
244|
245|이제 겨우 새벽 여섯 시. 이른 새벽에, 그것도 자다 깨서 먹는 아침이 반가울 리 없다.
246|
247|그러나 박지훈은 군말 없이 감사하다는 인사와 함께 수저를 들었다.
248|
249|“길드장님께서는 안 드십니까?”
250|
251|“난 이미 먹었네. 신경 쓰지 말고 마저 식사하게.”
252|
253|대수롭지 않게 대답한 그가 신문을 펼쳤다. 오늘 자 조간신문이다.
254|
255|1면에는 숙연한 얼굴로 고개 숙인 정장 차림의 장년인의 사진이 실려 있었다.
256|
257|
258|
259|故정현우 헌터의 빈소를 찾은 박태섭 명동 길드장. “그저 비통한 마음뿐, 유가족들에게 머리 숙여 사과.”
260|
261|
262|
263|박지훈은 그제야 왜 자신을 불렀는지 알 것 같았다.
264|
265|‘영감쟁이가 뿔이 났군.’
266|
267|컬러 사진 속 장년인과 똑 닮은 그가 신문에서 눈을 떼지 않은 채 물었다.
268|
269|“사진 어때. 잘 나왔나?”
270|
271|“예. 워낙 인물이 좋으시니까요.”
272|
273|“자네는 그게 문제야. 무슨 말을 해도 항상 빈말처럼 들리거든.”
274|
275|“진심입니다.”
276|
277|망설임 없는 대답에 장년인, 명동 길드장 박태섭의 눈썹이 치켜 올라갔다.
278|
279|그의 인내심이 끊어졌다는 신호였다.
280|
281|“정현우. 이 친구는 왜 죽였나?”
282|
283|올 게 왔군.
284|
285|박지훈은 조용히 수저를 내려놓으며 대답했다.
286|
287|“냄새를 맡았습니다.”
288|
289|“그럼 코를 막는 정도로 끝냈어야지.”
290|
291|“그건 명동 길드에서 해야 할 역할입니다. 제 역할은 구린내 맡은 놈들이 어딘가에서 떠벌리기 전에 목을 비트는 거고요.”
292|
293|“내 허락도 없이?”
294|
295|“허락도 받아야 합니까?”
296|
297|쾅!
298|
299|박태섭의 주먹이 식탁을 후려쳤다. 우지끈하는 소리와 함께 식탁이 부서지며 유리와 음식이 사방으로 튀었다.
300|
301|“길드장님!”
302|
303|황급히 달려온 경호원들을 기다리고 있던 것은 창노한 외침이었다.
304|
305|“모두 썩 물러가라! 내 지시가 있기 전까지는 한 발자국도 들어오지 마!”
306|
307|“……!”
308|
309|순간 멈칫한 이들이 허리를 숙인 뒤 물러났다.
310|
311|박지훈은 아무렇지 않게 손수건을 꺼내 얼굴에 튄 국물을 닦았다.
312|
313|“아쉽네요. 맛있었는데.”
314|
315|“이 젖비린내 나는 놈이 감히.”
316|
317|“어차피 피차 구린내 나는 건 마찬가진데, 젖비린내가 더해져 봤자 티도 안 납니다.”
318|
319|“내가 피 흘리며 세운 내 길드다. 그런데 네깟 놈이 말도 없이 길드원을 죽여?”
320|
321|“거 참. 길드장님.”
322|
323|주름 하나 없는 박지훈의 매끈한 미간이 찌푸려졌다.
324|
325|손에 쥔 손수건이 산산조각 난 테이블 잔해 위로 툭 떨어졌다.
326|
327|“그럼 어떡합니까?”
328|

Clicking his tongue softly, Park Jihoon climbed into the car. Perhaps because of the early hour, the roads were deserted.

[P103]
Some time later, the limousine glided to a stop in a part of Hannam-dong lined with luxury apartments and villas.

[P104]
Before them stood a massive mansion.

[P105]
One of the guards stationed along the stone wall ran over and bowed to Park Jihoon.

[P106]
“He’s waiting inside.”

[P107]
Park Jihoon passed through iron gates reminiscent of a European nobleman’s estate and crossed a garden larger than an athletic field before finally meeting the man who had summoned him.

[P108]
“Have you eaten?”

[P109]
The man was in his fifties, with hair that had gone half gray. His age belied his imposing physique, and well-developed chest muscles showed beneath his white robe.

[P110]
Park Jihoon bowed his head.

[P111]
“Not yet.”

[P112]
“Then come eat. The beef-and-radish soup turned out especially well today.”

[P113]
It was barely six in the morning. No one would welcome breakfast this early, especially after being dragged out of bed.

[P114]
Nevertheless, Park Jihoon thanked him and picked up his spoon without complaint.

[P115]
“Aren’t you eating, Guild Master?”

[P116]
“I’ve already eaten. Don’t mind me. Finish your meal.”

[P117]
The man casually unfolded a copy of that morning’s newspaper.

[P118]
The front page featured a photograph of a middle-aged man in a suit bowing his head solemnly.

[P119]
**Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, visits the wake of the late Hunter Jung Hyunwoo. “My heart is filled with grief. I bow my head and apologize to the bereaved family.”**

[P120]
Only then did Park Jihoon understand why he had been summoned.

[P121]
*The old geezer’s pissed.*

[P122]
The man, identical to the one in the color photograph, asked without looking up from the newspaper, “How’s the picture? Did I come out well?”

[P123]
“Yes. You’re naturally handsome.”

[P124]
“That’s your problem. No matter what you say, it always sounds like empty flattery.”

[P125]
“I mean it.”

[P126]
At the unhesitating answer, the middle-aged man—Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild—raised his eyebrows.

[P127]
It was a sign that his patience had run out.

[P128]
“Jung Hyunwoo. Why did you kill him?”

[P129]
*Here it comes.*

[P130]
Park Jihoon quietly set down his spoon.

[P131]
“He caught a whiff.”

[P132]
“Then you should have stopped at covering his nose.”

[P133]
“That was Myeongdong Guild’s job. Mine is to wring the necks of anyone who catches the stink before they can go blabbing about it.”

[P134]
“Without my permission?”

[P135]
“Did I need your permission?”

[P136]
Bang!

[P137]
Park Tae Seop slammed his fist into the dining table. The table shattered with a splintering crack, sending glass and food flying in every direction.

[P138]
“Guild Master!”

[P139]
The guards who came rushing in were met by a furious roar.

[P140]
“Get the hell out, all of you! Don’t take another step inside until I give the order!”

[P141]
“……!”

[P142]
They froze for a moment, then bowed and withdrew.

[P143]
Unperturbed, Park Jihoon pulled out a handkerchief and wiped the soup from his face.

[P144]
“What a shame. It was delicious.”

[P145]
“You insolent brat, still stinking of your mother’s milk…”

[P146]
“We both reek of something rotten anyway. A little milk on top won’t make any difference.”

[P147]
“I built this Guild with my own blood! And a little shit like you kills one of my Guild members without even telling me?”

[P148]
“Come now, Guild Master.”

[P149]
Park Jihoon’s smooth, unlined brow furrowed.

[P150]
The handkerchief slipped from his fingers and landed among the shattered remains of the table.

[P151]
“What else was I supposed to do?”

[P152]
“What did you say?”

[P153]
“Don’t you know how troublesome it gets when people who catch the stink start talking? One spark, and the whole house burns down. If it were only your house at risk, I wouldn’t have said a word. But the fire would spread to our side, so I stepped in.”

[P154]
“You still—!”

[P155]
“And I’d appreciate it if you got one thing straight. You’re a war hero who fought and bled during the Great Cataclysm? I’ll give you that. But claiming that Myeongdong Guild belongs to you is a bit…”

[P156]
Park Jihoon let out a short laugh and rose from his seat.

[P157]
“Thank you for breakfast. Though I barely managed a few spoonfuls.”

[P158]
Park Tae Seop trembled as he watched him.

[P159]
“Sit down.”

[P160]
“If you have anything else to say, call me. Keep this up, and I might lose my respect for you as a great senior.”

[P161]
“I said sit down.”

[P162]
The air around them churned violently.

[P163]
Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, was a hero forged by the Great Cataclysm and one of the country’s highest-ranking rankers.

[P164]
But Park Jihoon knew the man couldn’t lay a hand on him.

[P165]
“I’ll see you next time.”

[P166]
He bowed politely and was about to turn away when Park Tae Seop spoke again.

[P167]
“The sparks you scattered are about to burn the whole house down. You didn’t know that?”

[P168]
“What are you talking about? I handled Team Leader Jung’s matter thoroughly enough to prevent any loose talk.”

[P169]
“The Black Hunters. I heard they recently went after a D-rank Hunter from the Peace Guild.”

[P170]
Park Jihoon’s face stiffened.

[P171]
He instinctively realized that something had gone seriously wrong.

[P172]
“……What is it? What happened?”

[P173]
At that moment, the phone inside Park Jihoon’s coat pocket began to vibrate.

[P174]
As if in a trance, he pulled it out and stared darkly at the name filling the screen.

[P175]
**Jin Taekyung**

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 278

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃278화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|아름답던 2층 주택은 흉가(凶家)로 변해 있었다.
  6|
  7|수십 겹의 방어막이 멸염신권의 충격을 일부 흡수하지 않았다면 모두 잿더미가 되어 버렸을 것이다.
  8|
  9|그때, 등 뒤로 인기척이 가까워지더니 나직한 목소리가 귓가를 울렸다.
 10|
 11|“진태경 씨.”
 12|
 13|반쯤 그을린 소파에 앉아 있던 나는 고개를 돌리며 대답했다.
 14|
 15|“네.”
 16|
 17|최 팀장과 김 집사. 그리고 송송이다.
 18|
 19|나를 바라보는 그들의 눈빛은 복잡해 보였다. 정원에서부터 처참하게 널브러진 시신들을 봤으니 당연한 반응일지도 모른다.
 20|
 21|온통 피를 뒤집어쓴 내 몰골도 썩 좋아 보이진 않을 거고.
 22|
 23|송송이가 조심스럽게 물었다.
 24|
 25|“혹시, 전부 죽인 거야?”
 26|
 27|“응.”
 28|
 29|“……!”
 30|
 31|“농담이야. 항복한 놈들은 살려 뒀어.”
 32|
 33|부드럽게 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 34|
 35|“일단은.”
 36|
 37|송송이에게 한 대답이지만 최 팀장과 김 집사를 향한 말이기도 하다.
 38|
 39|최 팀장이 우려 섞인 표정으로 물었다.
 40|
 41|“다친 곳은 없습니까?”
 42|
 43|“보시다시피 멀쩡해요.”
 44|
 45|“생존자들은?”
 46|
 47|“한곳에 모아 놨습니다.”
 48|
 49|“아무런 조치도 없이 말입니까?”
 50|
 51|“물론 했죠. 앞으로 몇 시간 동안은 숨 쉬는 시체나 다름없으니까 안심하세요.”
 52|
 53|개인적인 조치라는 건 점혈이었다.
 54|
 55|아혈과 마혈, 수혈을 짚은 뒤 블랙 헌터들을 딱 하나 남은 방에 차곡차곡 처박아 뒀다.
 56|
 57|무력 진압을 하긴 했지만, 내가 무슨 피에 미친 살인귀도 아니고 항복하는 놈들까지 죽일 생각은 없었다.
 58|
 59|무엇보다 나중에 쓰임새가 있을 수도 있고.
 60|
 61|“잘하셨습니다. 그런데…….”
 62|
 63|최 팀장의 시선이 내 발밑에 쓰러져 있는 누군가를 향했다.
 64|
 65|“그건 누굽니까?”
 66|
 67|“이 집 주인이요.”
 68|
 69|발로 놈의 몸을 뒤집자 40대 남성의 모습이 드러났다.
 70|
 71|집주인이자 블랙 헌터들의 우두머리인 임영준이다.
 72|
 73|시체로 착각할 만큼 전신이 피범벅이었지만, 분명히 살아 있다. 그것도 상처 하나 없는 모습으로.
 74|
 75|놈을 살핀 김 집사가 알 만하다는 듯이 중얼거렸다.
 76|
 77|“포션을 썼군요. 그것도 여러 번 반복해서.”
 78|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
